chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hus-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id al-A'raj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the fasting one who tastes something and does not swallow it. He (peace be upon him) said: 'No'.
ai.seo_question: Does tasting food while fasting break the fast if you do not swallow it?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that incidental tasting for flavor assessment does not invalidate the fast, provided the substance is not swallowed, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that minor, non-nutritive intake is permissible. It highlights the distinction between deliberate consumption and accidental or functional tasting, a nuance often discussed in Usul al-Fiqh regarding the nullifiers of Sawm. The chain of transmission through prominent Kufan narrators underscores the reliability of this ruling in early Shia legal tradition.
